utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Karnavas: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Butler.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe we left off yesterday at a juncture where you had made a comment which had piqued my interest, but before we get to that, I want to revert to an earlier line of questioning and try to deconstruct, if it is possible, your answer. And so -- and this is with respect to the zone of responsibility. I will be referring to page 52 from the -- from yesterday's testimony, and I have copies. There's one available for the ELMO as well as one for you. And in fact there are two sets of copies, but anyway, if you could just briefly look at it at starts with page 54, it goes on to page 55 and then page 56. Now, I want to focus your attention and start with page 54. I'm just going to ask the question -- we won't go through the entire portion of it, but I believe I ask you -- I'm trying to pin you down and I'm asking you about the rules, whether they were adopted. Do you see that portion, around line 15?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then your answer is: "With respect to the combat regulations, the organisation of formation, the methodologies used in the command and staff process, the VRS, not only did they adopt the ones of the former JNA, but as the JNA dissolved in May of 1992, the VJ was formed. As the VJ modified some of those, the VRS tried to remain as much in step with that as well." Okay. You see that. Now, if you flip on to the next page, and this is where I am really interested in. I ask you to -- the question: "Okay. So I take it if we were to go into the regulations that we were applying -- that they were applying and that that had taken over the JNA, we would be able to find, for instance, the term 'zone of responsibility' for the brigades." And your answer is: "I believe that term either area or zone of responsibility will be found in the 1983 command and staff regulations." Do you recall being asked that question and giving that answer?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in fact I believe overnight you were going to look into the manual of those particular regulations to look for the term "zone of responsibility." Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I looked in the 1984 manual. I didn't know this was a specific question on tap for me to research.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And then we're going to deconstruct that question as well as the next one. The next one is -- goes as follows: "Okay. Now, in the rules setting up the brigade, is it that in the" -- "is that in the rules?" Answer, and here's your entire answer and then we're going to deconstruct it. "In the brigade rules, you are not going to generally find that because as a context by which most brigades were designed to fight in the JNA, certainly in 1984, brigades were not generally given a zone of operations or a zone of operations -- or an area of operations, they were given something more limited with respect to a frontage, an axis of advance. With respect to brigades, normally within the context of the 1984 regulations, TO units," and I suspect you're referring to -- you're going to tell us what that means, "which were given rear service-based operations, counter-insurgency or types of rear missions like that, those units could be given an area of responsibility. But for the actual combat operations, you didn't see that at brigade level." Next question: "Well, under the rules, if you know, what sort of zones were they given?" Answer: "Generally envisaged for the manoeuvre brigades under the 1984 rules, they were derived on a larger military context where a brigade would not necessarily be fighting alone. It was envisaged -- it would fight as either part of a parent division or when divisions went away were replaced by a brigade corps structure, that they would fight in context with a larger corps formation. So in that context, it was geared toward a more conventional setting." Now, I take it you recall making that statement?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, for the purposes of deconstructing this, I would like to show you a cleaner version which I have underlined for the convenience of everybody, and I would like to have this marked for identification purposes. This is --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I believe it would be D83.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could just look at it very briefly to see whether it comports with what we just read, but I'm going to go through it line by line in some respects to see if we can make sense of this answer.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume this is the page you want on the ELMO, sir?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Okay. Now, if we go with the first question your answer -- I say. I don't want to repeat it, but I'm asking for a zone of responsibility. You say: "I believe that the term either area or zone of responsibility will be found in the 1983 command and staff regulations." Now, do you -- can you tell us a little bit about what those regulations are all about.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1983 command and staff regulations are a series of regulations which define the aspects of military command within the former JNA. They define command, they define command relationships, they define staff relationships, they talk about in some great detail the command and staff and how it interfaces in various forms of combat operations to include offence, defence. So it's a very useful document with respect to fundamentally understanding the roles and responsibilities of a commander, command, staff, and how that all interrelates within the military decision-making process.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Now, this manual, however, which pretty much is a guidebook for commanders on how to command, does not articulate zones of responsibility, areas of operations, that's not the purpose of this, is it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I believe that in the context there it's discussed as being part of some of the control measures that will be made available.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I will go back and research that and try to find the specific notations. It wasn't something I did last night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, maybe you can do that during the break, but now that you mention control measures, yesterday we were talking about control measures and I posed a question which was: The zones of defence, zones of operation, were those not control measures? And I believe your answer was yes.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And so if we're trying to locate control measures, would we not then go to the rules, because that's where they are, in there.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the 1984 brigade rules, it defines the normative control measures for brigades, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by normative? Let's keep it plain?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very simply what it means is it defines the control measures that are used under ideal circumstances. Clearly like all forms of combat situations those need to be modified on the ground on the basis of the dictates of terrain, on the dictates of enemy situation and things of that nature. But for by and large the general purposes, those regulations define those various types of control measures under most circumstances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then you go on, because I'm trying to get to my answer, because I've asked you about zones of responsibility. Now the question comes again: "But in the rules setting up in the brigade, is that in the rules?" Now we're talking about the brigade rules of 1984. And here's your answer and we're going to go step by step. "In the brigade rules," we'll stick with one at a time, "you're not going to generally find that." Let's stop there. When you say "generally," I take it if we're not going to find it generally we're certainly not going to find it specifically. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, I disagree. The document which you showed me yesterday which was paragraph 13 specifically mentioned that phrase area of responsibility --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, I'm talking about a zone of responsibility --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. He's interrupting the witness and this matter, as far as I can see, has been gone through over and over again yesterday now we're going through what he went over and over again yesterday and this is potentially endless.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I think the answer in this transcript says area or zone of responsibility will be defined.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And it's true that this issue has been gone over yesterday, unless you have some specific point to make.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour, and the specific point that I'm making is we didn't receive an answer yesterday. And he just indicated The point where I showed him where he says area of responsibility, perhaps he can show us where is that in paragraph 13.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, area of operations. I misspoke on this one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see. There we go. I want to focus on zone of responsibility, because that is a term that you've used. Now -- and that is my question. So getting back to it, you say: "Not going to generally find it." And my question was: If it's generally not there, certainly specifically it would not be there. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I agree and I believe --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the answer yes --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. It's an interruption, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You have to be very patient. Let the witness finish his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour, I'm trying to get him home on time, but at this rate, I dare say - and I'm very serious about this - you asked me to streamline, but based on what I saw last night and what I have, I need two weeks with this gentleman. I'm very serious. And so if I'm going to get nonresponsive responses, I will take my time. I have no problem with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the answer to my question is yes. Specifically, it's not in there. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular context in these regulations, I don't believe the phrase "zone of responsibility" is in there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean in this context, is the word "zone of responsibility" in there? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, it isn't in there and as we've discussed I used those phrases interchangeably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we do have a zone of operations, though, don't we?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are areas and zones of operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is not in a general sense, that's in a specific sense in the rules. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area of operations and the zone of operations are specific in the rules and they are different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So the answer again to my question is yes?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you say "generally," define that word "generally" so that at least I have a general understanding of what you mean.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, as I've indicated with looking at the former JNA regulations and their applicability down the line to the VRS, I also take into account the fact that I've been reading military documents from the VRS for five years where these issues are discussed. So, again, I can't do my analysis and I don't do my analysis by specifically looking at one document or one regulation, I lay it out in the general context. And as we have discussed, while these are the baseline regulations and that they were followed as much as practicable by the VRS, the VRS did migrate from them based on the situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: So when I use the phrase "generally," I'm using it as a way to indicate the broader context of all the documents I've reviewed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you go: "Because as a context by which," I guess that's the general that you're talking about, generally and now it's the general context. "As a context by which" -- I'm on number 2; we'll do number 2 and 3 together. "As a context by which most brigades were designed to fight in the JNA." Now, what are you talking about when you say "context" and "most brigades" and who are those "most brigades," because I have a rule on brigades.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you will note from the brigade rules, and under the larger context of All People's Defence, the general strategy of that, given the fact that in the larger context they had NATO on one side and the Warsaw Alliance on the other. Their broader strategy was that the active forces of the JNA would defend the perimeters of the country as much as possible and that the brigades that were formed under the TO when they were mobilised as such would be the next component of the armed forces and would conduct whatever guerilla or insurgency war against an occupying force. When I talk about"most brigades" in this context, the JNA recognised that the circumstances how a regular infantry brigade or a mechanised brigade or an armoured brigade or even a naval infantry brigade would fight versus how a light infantry brigade in an occupied territory would fight would be different. So that's what I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said "occupied territory". First of all, let's get clear on one thing. Territorial Defence, they're not a part of the JNA, are they?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're a part of the armed forces, but they're not specifically a part of the JNA in this context.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They're not under the JNA?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the 1984 context, no, sir. I mean, at that time. At a point in time further during the war, some elements do become and I didn't want to get into that --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're talking about the 1984 --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1984, it's a separate concept.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And were talking about the Territorial Defence kicking in when the land is occupied; correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And that means when enemy troops are in Belgrade, for instance, and now you're going to do what the Iraqis are doing to the allied forces in Baghdad. They're fighting within. And that's where the Territorial Defence kicks in. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is how it was designed, yes, sir. But it's not quite that isolated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, it is a more flowing process because, as indicated in the brigade roles, they also envision, in some cases, other regular JNA formations would be part and parcel to that general resistance programme.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're going to get to that, we're going to get to that. But these brigade rules were designed for brigades in the JNA. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were designed for brigades within the JNA. However, I'm not sure how you can differentiate that insomuch as the officers and soldiers, as we discussed yesterday, who were the TO were in fact members who served in the JNA and their officers were active JNA. There's not two different sets of doctrine on this one, or manuals. It is one set of combat regulations designed for the broader context.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. You would agree --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would agree there was no occupation going on at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about in 1995? Was Bratunac occupied by the Muslim forces, the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just answer the question.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe that they would consider some portions of the Bratunac municipality that were occupied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was ultimately when they established -- when the VRS established and gave that zone of responsibility to the Bratunac Brigade in November 1992, if you look at that on a map and look at the part that they actually controlled, I believe the VRS indicates that they probably controlled less than a quarter of that territory and it was still given to the Bratunac Brigade as their zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're going to get to the map. But then you go on and you say: "Certainly in 1994 brigades were -- 5, not generally given a zone of operation or area of area of operation." So now we have the new rules in 1984. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You said 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 1984, okay?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1984 rules, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now the new rules come in?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume they're new rules. I have not seen an earlier set.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we're dealing about these rules --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down. It is impossible to follow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're talking about these rules. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're stating here that the brigades were not generally given a zone of operation or an area of operation. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what you said?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that what you said? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not -- I did say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, if you look at the rules, and I believe we looked at them yesterday, and in fact, I said that they should always have a zone of operation, and you quarrelled with me a little bit because you said it says shall. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Reminding of quarrels yesterday really is not a question. We're stuck in 1984 in a Orwellian nightmare. If we could get on to something relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm impeaching his witness, that's what I'm doing. And if he doesn't like it he should just prep his witness differently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, as you understand we still remember very clearly the debate yesterday about that rule. So there's no need to revisit it at this moment, just move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I want to pin him down. I want to pin him down on this, because he says one thing, we go to the rules. He said "zone" today that are in the rules -- or area and it wasn't -- area of responsibility and it's not in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't think there's any dispute about that "shall," because we discuss it already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now that we all know that the rule says shall, you agree with me that this is incorrect when you say not generally given a zone of operation.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Clearly, I misspoke. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just didn't misspeak, you were absolutely 100 per cent wrong.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was absolutely 100 per cent wrong, sir, in that respect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Thank you for that admission. Now, in fact, as I understand it they're even supposed to have a line of defence, a zone of defence. I think if we go to paragraph on page 126 of the rules, paragraph 483.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it's amazing how clear it is, how direct. "A brigade is always assigned a defence zone." It says that right there. Right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- and yesterday, as you will recall when we were talking about zone of operations, I told you based on the way it was formulated in paragraph 3, zone of defence was inclusive in zone of operation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a normal practice with that respect that in any mission a commander is going to plan to have to transition into defence, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's move on. Then you say -- okay, you said: "They were not generally given a zone of operation or an area of operation, they were given something more limited with respect to a frontage and axis of advance." Now, it seems to me that what you're saying here is not only were they not given a zone of responsibility, not only were they not given a zone of operation, but they were given something even much lesser than that, which at least from your description sounds something more like a zone of defence?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe in this context where I'm referring to those specific axes, I believe that those are found with respect to offensive operations, not defensive ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Come again?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I make the observation where we're talking about a specific axes that a unit is given, in those general respects, those are more associated with offensive operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I guess it is technically possible for a unit to defend along an axis, it's usually not couched as such.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then yesterday I asked you about -- remember when we were talking about the zone of defences and zone of operation, that it would have to be so far forward and so far back, do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall your answer when you said it all depends on mission?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on mission, terrain and other variables.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I asked you if there were any other rules dictating that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I believe I referred back to this very portion, the defence zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, if we go back to paragraph 484, it would appear that we do have some guidance in these very rules --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- guiding the brigade commander, right? And in fact they're fairly specific; between 10 to 15 kilometres, and on mountainous grounds it would be 20 kilometres wide. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the width, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the rules do indeed envisage and point out, specify, the -- how far forward, how far back these zones would be. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. And again as we discussed yesterday, they even go into the brigade rear area and give the guidelines or the normal establishment of what the brigade rear area would be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the rear area doesn't go all the way to the boundaries of the municipality, and in this case it would be the Drina river?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I would note again in this particular document where it discusses that rear, it bases the rear on the depth required in order to properly set your fire support and properly set your logistics. That is normally envisioned within the brigade regulations. And I read it last night as I believe roughly 8 to 10 or 15 to 20 kilometres from the forward line of defence. So again how they are modified with respect to practical reality --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you don't mind, Mr. Butler, if you want to put something on the ELMO, you can ask us or ask permission, but I believe I'm doing cross, it's not direct. I run the show when I'm doing cross, not you. Now if you want to put something on the ELMO for instructional purposes, please tell us what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what this was paragraph 498, which discusses the logistics of support forces --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and notes where the depth of the brigade zone is. And the point that I'm trying to illustrate on this one is clearly that it is beyond 15 kilometres from the forward defence line to the Drina river, so again the dictates of terrain and national boundaries play an important role in defining all of these lines. It's just not rote from the book.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- but, again if we refer back to the Bratunac Brigade, it was your testimony that they were in a defensive or a static posture, and one would assume, would they not, that while they were there for all those years they had a certain amount of forward ground that they had to be responsible for and a certain amount of ground in the back. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that would still remain more or less the same, given the -- their involvement in the attack on Srebrenica as specified of what their involvement would be by the preparatory order handed down to them by the Drina Corps. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. That rear zone should not have changed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Moving along, you say with respect to brigades: "Normally in the context of the 1984 regulations," and I take it you're speaking about these rules, "TO units," Territorial Defence units, "which were given rear operations bases, counter-insurgency, or types of rear missions like that, those units would be given an area of responsibility." Now, that's your answer, correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's when All People's Defence kicks in?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe I know the answer to whether it specifically kicks in or how that works. It was envisioned under these rules that active JNA forces and TO forces would be operating in at least an integrated manner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When their land was occupied by enemy forces?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I would also presume that in the event for whatever reason the JNA elected to take offensive operations, it would have been prudent to have used the TO to provide the same rear area security. So I don't think it's exclusive to an occupation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The TOs, were they not designed as a means of the people, All People's Defence, the people themselves, that they would mount a resistance from within if they were occupied?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So it's not about an offensive operation, it's about a defensive operation. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would disagree. I would say it's an integrated operation between the JNA and TO, regardless of the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And then you go on and you say: "But for the actual combat operations, you didn't see that at the brigade level." What didn't you see at the brigade level? That I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Discussing it -- wait a second.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may want to refer to your earlier --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, discussing it in the context that I brought out today, it -- because again it was envisioned that the active components of the JNA would engage as much as possible with -- in conventional combat where the TO units, which were rather ill-suited for that, would be involved in more traditional military functions with respect to rear area operations and rear area security. So that is why I envisioned or that is why, you know, when I say I envisioned that, it wasn't a context where I didn't want to imply that they were going to use standard infantry brigades to conduct rear area operations when they had other forces available.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, next question. I'm still trying to get an answer to my initial question which was on zone of responsibility. We talked about everything but that. Then we go on: "Well, under the rules, if you know, what sort of zones were they given?" And your answer: "Generally," that pops up again, "generally envisage for the two," number two I have, "manoeuvre brigades under the 1984 rules." Now, were the 1984 rules different, do they differentiate between manoeuvre brigades and non-manoeuvre brigades?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe that's a phraseology on my part. When I refer to manoeuvre brigades, I am referring to the armoured or the mechanised infantry, motorised types of brigades, even the light one that has motorised support, as opposed to the light infantry brigade that we see with a more static environment or a more static position. So that's where I use the phrase "manoeuvre". Again, I apologise if that's confusing. It is a take-off on some of the VRS terminology where they use the phrase "manoeuvre brigades".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These rules, sir, these rules don't make any distinction and in fact when we talk even about light infantry brigades, we're really talking about the size and the structure and the resources that they have. But as far as what they're -- when we're talking about zones of operation and zones of defence, really these rules apply to all the brigades, do they not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The general principles and the rules do apply to all the brigades, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they make no distinctions of such a thing as manoeuvre brigade that you injected into the conversation yesterday, which may sound esoteric, it may sound lofty, but at the end of the day when we pin you down, it really doesn't make any difference whether we use that word or don't use it at all. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would disagree because the regulation do delineate that -- it is envisioned that some units, the light infantry brigades as an example, would not normally have many of the same offensive functions that other formations are expected to have, such as the motorised or mechanised infantry. So that's the differential that I'm trying to make. Because of the organisation of the brigade, there are expectations that it is more suited for one mission as opposed to another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I'm going back to the zone. This whole conversation is taking place around the zone, the zone of responsibility, that you injected into -- you're sticking with that phrase. So with respect to zones, manoeuvre or non-manoeuvre has no meaning in this context, does it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this context it would not be a differential because JNA forces, if they were assigned an area of operations in occupied territory would be expected to operate as other forces would whether they be JNA or TO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I hope that the counsel and the witness could look at the screen. When the transcript is finished, you may ask or answer the question, otherwise you give a very difficult time to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, moving along, you say, and I'll start again: "Generally envisage for the manoeuvre brigades under the 1984 rules, they were derived on a larger military context where." "Derived on a larger military context," what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you complete the sentence, I think it's explanatory. It indicates that as envisioned under the brigade rules as well as the corps rules, the brigades are envisioned to fight as part of a larger entity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But doesn't -- okay. So we read -- we'll complete the sentence. "Derived on a larger military context where a brigade would not necessarily be fighting alone." Well, help me out here, why would a brigade be fighting alone? It's part of a corps, is it not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, but referring back to these regulations, there are references where it is envisioned that a brigade that was isolated behind enemy lines or in occupied territory might have to conduct independent operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what does that have to do with a zone of responsibility? Nothing, correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has to do with an area of operations, but nothing with the zone of responsibility, and again as I've noted, that's not probably not the best term to use.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly with respect to the 1984 regulations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you would agree with me, would you not, that that first sentence of that answer doesn't help us and doesn't answer the question that I was asking?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I disagree because I think in the context, certainly the context that I understood the question, when we're talking about setting up axis and unit frontages, those are relevant issues.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. Then you go on the next sentence, number 6: "It was envisaged it would fight as either a," that's my part, "a part of a parent division or when divisions went away and were replaced by a brigade corps structure, that they would fight in context with a larger corps formation." Again, what are you trying to say with respect to a zone? How does that help us define whether the rules here designate a zone of responsibility, a term which is not found in the rules?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would revert back to my prior answer, again taking in context with -- that a brigade and the control measures placed on that brigade are not going to be done in isolation, they're going to be done in the context of part of a larger whole, be it a division or be it a corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, again, I just -- I'm having a hard time understanding your English, maybe. But how does this sentence, even with the earlier sentence, how does that answer my question which says: "Well, under the rules, if you know, what sort of zones were they given?" And I originally started with the zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, again in the context that we've been discussing it, I'm looking at it along the variable issue of depending on the brigade's mission and depending on the other forces available. Now, again, we've already discussed that that's probably not the best phrase to use and certainly doesn't exist in the regulation. So I said, when I'm using that phrase, I'm using it in that context. We can use the more appropriate phrase zone of operations, and I believe the answer slips right in there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But if we go to the zone of operations, then we go to the definition in the rules and then we have some guidance. And then when we're discussing the zone of operations, at least we can be on the same wavelength, the same channel of communications. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, in this respect the rules do outline those, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Whereas if we're talking about zones of responsibility, especially in your context in the description that you have given, which encompassed the geographical border of municipalities, more or less, then we run into trouble, don't we, because we have no guidance, at least in the rules. I'm just sticking with the rules right now?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specific to the rules, you are correct. And as I noted yesterday, specific to the issues of the establishment of the zones in the Drina Corps, that I do not have a Drina Corps document which specifically articulates what's supposed to be envisioned in those zones of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So then you finally say: "So in that context, it was geared toward a more conventional setting." Now, again forgive me, but I'm desperately trying to figure out what you're saying here, because I ask about what a zone is and then I ask you under the rules what the zones are, and then you give this answer which seems to be a non sequitur.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Improper question. He's taking a piece of a question out of the context of a whole day's of cross-examination and he's calling it non sequitur or whatever, and entering into his own personal comments on it. This is not cross-examination. I don't know what it is, but I can tell you it's -- objection to the form of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, if you don't understand the answer by this witness from yesterday, just put your question there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm asking him to work with me to help me out. He's working with me. I'm desperately trying to figure this one out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you help us out when you say: "So, in that context," I take it when you say "that context," we're talking about the earlier context?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about the 1984 regulation context.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And to answer the rest of the question, where I say: "conventional setting," when you look at the 1984 brigade rules, they are clearly designed for more, in a military parlance, conventional military operations, attack, defence, those types of issues. While there is some language which reflects what we would consider unconventional warfare operations or resistance operations, that is what I mean when I say the phrase conventional setting, what would normally be referred to as medium-intensity combat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I think we can move on to another segment. Let me clarify that. While we're still on zone of responsibility, I thought I would direct all of our attention to page 5 of your narrative, your revised narrative.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I have to apologise to the interpreters for speaking too fast. I tend to be a little hyper in the morning -- but in the evening as well, so ... I believe this has been marked for identification purposes as P358.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have it, sir?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it's up on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if we look at it, we're not going to go through the entire narrative. I'd love to, I don't have a week or two, but just a little vignette. If we look at paragraph 2.3.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this is the command report and not the narrative, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if you tagged an exhibit number to it, that's why I raise it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry about that. It's the command report. We make mistakes as well. Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If we look at --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, the command report's 357, just for your record.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 357, okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we look at 2.3, we see here, and I'll just read it, it's short: "Moreover, with respect to organising collaboration within the brigade zone of operations," and then it ends again with "within the zone of operations." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It would appear here that you're using the correct terminology, phraseology, whatever we want to call it. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact you even footnote it. Now, if we go to 2.4, immediately below, I don't need to read it, but at the last it ends, the sentence ends with: "Zone of responsibility." And we have a footnote again. Now, if you could go to the footnote and get it handy so you have it readily available.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I'll read the sentence and see what we can make of it. "He continues to remain individually responsible and accountable for the planning and conduct of military operations within his designated zone of responsibility." Question: Are you making a distinction between zone of operation, a term which is found and grounded well within the rules, and zone of responsibility here?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular instance, I believe since I'm phrasing it with this designated, I'm using it as the context of zone of operations, that would probably be the more accurate phrase to use on that one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I ask you what motivated you to put zone of responsibility, because when we hear this zone of responsibility, we envisage something much larger than zone of operation.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, the context of that is that in the VRS, zones of responsibility existed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And ultimately we are talking about a brigade commander in the VRS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's look at the footnote and see if the footnote corresponds to the body, because I would assume that the footnote --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to put the paragraph up on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can put it up, you can certainly put it up, 115. Now, do you see anywhere there zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. Most of it's just related to the brigade commander's exclusive rights for command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So if one were to read this and not check the footnote, as many people tend to do, unless they have a fetish with footnotes, they would find that this is a clear misrepresentation, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe so, sir. And again, you could read the entire paragraph, and I've copied it verbatim in paragraph 2.1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we're going to stick with this.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're going to stick with this.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: So again while I'm tying that particular representation of a commander's responsibility, again I'm also noting the fact that in 1995 within the brigade structure, it did expand. And while I'm not deliberately trying to misrepresent anything, I recognise under your argument I could have done a more accurate job in citing it, and I should have cited some of the specific zone of responsibility documents to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Using your own analytical skills, your analysis and synthesis, one might get the impression or a logical conclusion could be reached that you were trying to pull a fast one on this one, couldn't they? I'm not saying that you were, but they could reach the conclusion based on the same skills of analysis and synthesis that you have done in this particular case.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, just to prevent that very thing, that is why I work hard as possible to take direct lifts from the regulations where possible. I understand given my own Western military background, that there are going to be times when I may inaccurately paraphrase the difference between a JNA regulation and a Western one. That is why I generally adopt the practice. I trust that there is nothing nefarious involved in that, but I will leave, of course, that up to the Court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting that. It may be a Freudian slip. Maybe you just want to wish that there is a zone of responsibility for a brigade commander and by putting it in, somehow we will all believe by reading this, unless we go to the footnote, that somehow in what is cited as an authority, zone of responsibility is indeed designated to a brigade commander. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the context of the VRS, it is, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, please point the text to me. You have cited 115.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like I said, in this context it was not properly cited, and I should have used some VRS citation. But again it wasn't my desire to do that insomuch as I didn't think zone of responsibility was the optimum phrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think both of you are getting excited again. Just look at the screen, and if the transcript is finished, then begin your question or answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you deliberately chose to inject a term, because this is the first time that we see it in this document when immediately above it you used the correct term, zone of operation. Why?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I noted it was an improper use of phraseology on my part. I should not have done that. I should have used the proper term. And if I was going to use the term "zone of responsibility," I should have done a better job of citing a document to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which document might you have cited that says that a brigade commander has a zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are a number of VRS documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Cite them, please, the ones that say that a brigade commander is assigned a zone of responsibility in the context in which you have indicated to us, that is, that it corresponds with the borders of a municipality?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, the first document that I would use, and I was looking at it yesterday, would be the map reference from the VRS Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's stick with that one. Just a few questions on that.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we going to that map, sir?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we don't actually have to physically get it. Military folks like maps, but I don't feel comfortable when I'm around them.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You don't have to call them field artillery, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that map, when was that generated?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that map was generated sometime in late 1992/early 1993, because as I recall the corps commander is still identified as Colonel Zivanovic and not General Zivanovic, and in mid-1993, he was promoted to General Major, so that's what I use to make that analysis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, he had been a colonel for quite some time, had he not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Butler has obviously said he's more comfortable dealing with the map, if he's going to get particular questions about it --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I haven't got to the map yet. I'm entitled to do my cross the way I want to. I haven't asked him to fetch the map yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, we are not military experts, but if there's a map there, it would be of great help to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. I'm not trying to avoid getting to the map. But I was asking some preparatory questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But if it helps, get the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If the gentleman feels more comfortable with the map, far be it of me to deprive him of that comfort.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, he has made this massive thing all morning that there is no evidence of zone of responsibility. When Mr. Butler cites the first document to that map, he won't even let Mr. Butler get it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, I said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think I have made a ruling on this issue. We are not going to debate it any more. Just put the map on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We have the map, Your Honour. Nobody's trying to hide the ball on this side of the table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No. I'm not blaming you on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, before we get to the map, can I ask you a few questions that aren't related directly to the locations, the coordinates on the map?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would that be okay with you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say getting back that you had indicated that you made a reference that you thought this was created sometime in late 1992/beginning 1993, because as a frame of reference you used Colonel Zivanovic, his rank, as a point of departure?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because had he said, since, major general, then we would know at least when he had been appointed. We could say somewhere between this period and that period. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, at some point he became a general. Right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe he became a general major in mid-1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And at this point he was the commander of the Drina Corps while he was still a colonel?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I take it nothing changed with respect to the Drina Corps from 1992 to 1995?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that respect, sir, one of the things -- obviously safe areas were installed, there were some changes in the border, but with respect to the Bratunac Brigade issue, one of the most useful documents that I went back to track that was the history of the Bratunac Brigade, which was drafted by the Bratunac Brigade, which defines a lot of those issues.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: So with respect to these issues, there don't appear to be substantive changes until after the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, my question was about the Drina Corps. And then you went on about the Bratunac Brigade. So if we could just go step by step on this. All right. Now, I asked you if things happen with respect to the Drina Corps between 1992 and 1995, and you said something about safe areas. What are you referring to safe areas? What is that about?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, with respect to the Drina Corps in their zone, the UN established three safe areas that were either all or in part of the Drina Corps zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, here I notice -- you're not using the words zone of responsibility, a term which I believe you will find in the rules concerning the corps. Is there a particular reason why you're refraining from using that term, the correct term, zone of responsibility, or the complete term?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I believe you're correct. It is in the corps rules and that would be the appropriate term to use.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact, as I understand it, a corps has a geographical region as their zone?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the broader JNA practice and it was the VRS practice as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the Drina Corps would also have, if we could look on the map we could see exactly what section of the RS was their particular designated zone that they were responsible for. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And within that zone, you had various brigades situated in various places, strategic places, depending on what was happening at any particular time during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with respect to the Drina Corps, we know, at least with respect to two brigades, and you're going to fill us in on some of the others, they had lines that dated back from 1992 all the way to the conflict. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe if you're referring from May of 1992 to the beginning --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the attack on Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The lines that the Drina Corps had when they were formed in 1992, in some parts, were essentially the lines that they had adopted from the old units that were operating in that area before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did the line for the Bratunac Brigade change at all when Srebrenica was declared a safe zone?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I recall correctly, there were some minor changes in the lines back and forth. I believe that the VRS had actually advanced a lot closer to the town and some of the other areas, and as a result of the designation of the safe area, that some VRS forces had to withdraw to other locations outside of the established boundaries. I'm not sure how significant those movements were, but I do believe that they were much closer than the boundaries of the safe area were delineated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any point in time between 1992 and 1993 where ground was lost by both sides, some gained, eventually they lost it, do you understand what I'm talking about, with respect to Srebrenica and Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to Srebrenica and Bratunac, 1992 and 1993 was the most fluid part of that conflict. And it was also the period where the brigade suffered the most intense casualties. At one point in 1992, in the end -- by the beginning of 1993, the only territory that was held by the Bratunac Brigade was a small area around the town of Bratunac itself, because of the operations of -- at that time it was known as Operation Group 8, the Bosnian Muslims. By a few months later they managed to, with help from other units of the Drina Corps and the VRS, they greatly increased their territory. So it's almost on a day-by-day basis during that period in question that the lines are changing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So if I understand you correctly, at some point the Muslim army, the 28th Division, or whatever they might have been called at that point, had advanced or had taken land, and then at some point they lost it and they had to retreat towards Srebrenica. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at one point they were the advancing force and at another point they were the retreating force?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the UN came in and set up the enclave?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that this map was designed or marked at the end of 1992/beginning of 1993. Is there a particular reason why you chose towards the end of 1992 and not the middle or the beginning?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fact that the map is designated by General Zivanovic on the left-hand corner, and knowing that General Zivanovic did not - sorry, at this time Colonel Zivanovic, my mistake - did not become commander of the Drina Corps until 1992, that's why I caveat that line as with respect to this map from November 1992 to approximately mid-1993. That was my motivator.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at least we have a ballpark figure. So in -- when this map was drawn, what about the other brigades in the Drina Corps that were located at or near that area? Where were -- had they been formed?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Zvornik Infantry Brigade had been formed -- if we take November 1992 as a point in time, the Infantry Brigade or the Zvornik Infantry Brigade was organised as a light infantry brigade and it had been formed. The unit called the Vlasenica Brigade did not exist as such, it was more of an amalgamation of the Vlasenica and Milici units. It may have been called a brigade structure. I believe they called it the Vlasenica Brigade. It later broke into two separate units. The Birac Brigade existed in the Sekovici area. The 2nd Romanija Brigade was withdrawn from the Sarajevo Romanija Corps and reassigned to the Drina Corps. And in the south there were essentially five light infantry brigades in the areas between Rogatica, Visegrad, and the Gorazde area. So in that context, the brigades roughly existed as light infantry brigades, and then the Drina Corps tied them all together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say "at this time," are we talking about --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: November 1992, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wasn't sure whether - and I apologise - whether you said anything about the Milici Brigade. Had that been formed by that point in time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe -- I'll just -- wait a second. The Milici Brigade at that time, I believe, was still an integrated part of the Vlasenica Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we get to the map, because we're going to -- that's a whole separate line of questioning, we can break here if it's convenient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: *** Kindly slow down for the record***

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You see a sentence there in the transcript, "kindly slow down for the record".

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I didn't notice it, but I do notice it now. Again, my apologies to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Butler, now we're in your terrain with the map. So I understand that this is the map that you believe is one of the pieces that demonstrates to you that there was indeed a zone of responsibility in a geographical sense for the light infantry brigade of Bratunac. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. In the sense that it's associated with that brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I left off by asking you whether the Milici Brigade had been formed at this point in time and you seemed to be somewhat uncertain. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I actually did check that over the break because I didn't want to misspeak on this issue, and as it turns out, as the way that the units were being organised, the Milici Brigade did not exist, per se, as an independent entity, certainly during the production of this map. The Vlasenica Brigade also generally didn't exist; it was incorporated into the larger unit known as the Birac Brigade. And sometime in March of 1993, according to the documents that I have, is the first time that I see a reference to a Vlasenica/Milici Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are those documents post-advancement of General Zivanovic; in other words, from colonel to general?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not believe so, sir, I believe he would still be a colonel at this time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I take it once those brigades were formed, they would be given in your parlance, not mine, a zone of responsibility. Correct? I mean just in the theoretical, in the general sense, in the context of what we've been speaking of.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the practice that existed within the VRS at the time, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So -- and I take it if this map was generated prior to those brigades being formed, using military logic, a term which I believe you have used before, that this map should be modified, should it not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to additional zones being created, there is the possibility that the map would be modified to reflect that, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Because now we have additional brigades that will have their own zones of responsibility, by your terms, and I guess my question would be: Could you point those out to us on this particular map, where their zones of responsibility would be with respect to the area that's darkened, which I assume, which I assume, is what you believe that the Bratunac Brigade zone of responsibility was at the time of the attack on Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this particular map -- I guess I'll go from this side. Representing to the west of the Bratunac Brigade zone, this is, if my Cyrillic is correct on this one, I believe is the Birac -- or Bircanska Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You're correct on that.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This particular piece is the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And to the south, Separate Battalion Skelani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Might I ask, does the Office of the Prosecution have this map blown up or is this the only one that we have?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I believe Mr. McCloskey is signalling me, but I can't read --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Oh, he wishes for me to designate that we're now looking at what has been marked as P369.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe what we have -- there is no blow-up. This is actually a colour reproduction in scale.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, before looking -- we don't actually have to see it at this point, but if we look at it could you tell us exactly -- would you be able to mark on it so we can visualise where their zones, not lines of defence or zones of operations, but where their zones of responsibility would be, these newly created brigades that came into existence subsequent to the making of this map by Colonel Zivanovic back in 1992, perhaps early 1993.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be precise, there is a document from the Milici Brigade which is their semi-annual combat report which defines that. And I'd have to dovetail that with the map. I don't want to make just rough representations, if I don't have to on this particular instance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me just ask --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe - to finish the question though - I don't believe that there were substantive changes with respect to the zone of the Milici Brigade when it was incorporated. And I believe that, for the most part, it may have carved off a kilometre. I guess maybe I should put the map up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pointing at P369.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether it used the same western, south-western boundary as the boundary for theirs or not. I mean, that is something that we do have the information and we can correspond it on the map. But roughly speaking, the Milici Brigade would have had -- they would have been put in this area right here and this would have been their designated zone. So the answer is I can overlay it at a point in time; we do have the data to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can leave it like that for now. Well, I mean, you were keen on designating a zone of responsibility for the Bratunac Brigade. I would assume that at some point you sat down, being a military expert and knowing how to read maps, you must have looked at it and tried to pinpoint the coordinates to see where the one zone of responsibility ended and where the other one began. Was that done?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that respect where I pinpointed and overlaid the coordinates, I did not do that with respect to the Milici Brigade. The documents I used to do that was the war history of the Bratunac Brigade which identifies those points, because I did do the effort to look and see if those lines had changed over time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But again I hate to be picky about this, but with respect to the map, because you have a map and you say this map is one of the pieces of documents that you relied on in coming up with this term "zone of responsibility," which is not in the rules. And of course it does say zone of responsibility on top of the map, does it not? I mean, I don't know if you know Srpski.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not well. I've got the "zona" part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that that actually said "zone of responsibility," you wouldn't fight me on that, would you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you knew at this point, at least -- during your research you learned that when this map was prepared, two brigades did not exist, which would fit well into this map and they would -- these brigades bordered, if I could use that term loosely, where the Bratunac Brigade would have been located, if indeed this was their zone of responsibility. So my question again is: Did you ever plot it out on the map to see whether the zones overlap with respect to this map, since again we don't have a fixed time when this map was drawn and we know that there was a lot of events going on between 1992 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. Given the fact that the Bratunac data didn't indicate a change, I did not dovetail it with the Milici data to see if there was an overlap in the zones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that the Bratunac Brigade did not indicate a change. Well, are you suggesting that once two other battalions -- brigades were formed that would not have in any way changed the situation for the Bratunac Brigade with respect to what their zones of operations would have been? You see, I'm using my term "operations," as opposed to the global term "responsibility."

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I expected, had it changed, it would have been reflected in the Bratunac Brigade records which show those.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What -- you're a careful analyst and you told us you want to go -- you want to look at all the available data, so you would try to collate the data to see whether it fits neatly together, because sometimes you have pieces missing. So in this instance may I ask why, given that you had several years to work on this, why you never looked at the Milici Brigade coordinates on the map to see if there was an overlay, sort of a Venn diagram, if you recall that from our school years and geometry, in which case had they overlapped it would appear that two zones of responsibility or two brigades are sharing their own zone of responsibility. Do you follow what I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I have the thrust of the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the answer is because, as I've indicated before, I don't view - and it's not reflected as a result of documents - that the zone of responsibility of a unit is a crucial issue with respect to command and control of subordinate formations. The VRS in their documents, and my analysis of those, does not tie with respect to military units command and control of those units just because they happen to be in a zone at a point in time. So with respect, until the issue came up several days ago, where apparently that was a point of contention, the absolute boundaries with respect to these areas -- or these zones of -- or zone of responsibility, given my prior knowledge that this zone was designated with respect to the more broader issues of support, recruitment and everything else, I don't believe that the physical designation of a zone is this, is a key issue with respect to a commander and his role in subordinate formations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. We don't have time to deconstruct this entire answer. Perhaps maybe tomorrow, but for right now the answer to my question is: You didn't think it was necessary to check whether the Milici Brigade and the Skelani Brigade, when they were formed, whether their zones of responsibility overlapped this designated area, which would then give us some indication that perhaps things might have changed as a result of the passage of time and the development of the JNA -- of the VRS and the Drina Corps in particular.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. With respect to my analysis, I didn't believe it was relevant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right.
