So hypothetically speaking, if we were to learn if -- that the Milici Brigade and the Skelani Brigade zone of responsibility, a term that you use, in the context in which you have put it, which is not in the rules, would seem to overlap part of this area that is designated as a zone of responsibility for the Bratunac Brigade, that would not give you any sense of discomfort as an analyst?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to the establishment of command and control, it wouldn't. As an analyst, on a more broad level of understanding the context, it would be an interesting fact to know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now when you say "command and control," I take it because of our conversation yesterday that if within this designated area you have other units, be they from the Milici, Skelani, or the TG 1 unit that led the attack on Srebrenica, if they're operating within this geographical sphere, that the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, since he has no command and control over those units, he could not be held responsible for any of their acts?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it would be an improper objection at this point in time, and if so, I would like the witness to exit the courtroom. I don't want any -- it's a proper question. It deals with the map. It's in a different context, and there's no reason to object. The question was very specific.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could I say a few words?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, of course, always.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, your question, I believe, is proper, but the last part of that problem has some problems. This witness is a military expert and is not a legal expert. There may be some interpretations about the word "responsibility" for any of their acts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If you could rephrase it, I would be very appreciative.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will do that, with that point, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, let me hear Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't think you'll mind, Mr. Karnavas. Mr. Butler has spoken, as you're aware of, responsibility in the military sense and discussed those regulations. So my point is the same as Your Honour's, if it's to the military responsibility, that's a fair question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Point taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: To the legal responsibility, I think we have others --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I can see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think Mr. Karnavas already gets the gist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I throw my hands up, I concede.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You use the military term "command and control". Correct? So in that context if other units are there in this geographical sphere, the commander of the Bratunac Brigade would not have any command and control over them, would he, unless they were attached or resubordinate -- well, I believe you say resubordinated is attached or subordinated to the Bratunac Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly speaking, unless the superior put them directly in an order put them under his command and control, that he would not have command and control over them. That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, in your earlier answer you gave us a gem, what I would call, and I want to develop that a little bit. Because I think that you indicated about resources, that the brigade could draw resources from. Might you have been saying that from this geographical region, keeping in mind your earlier answer about the TOs, Territorial Defence, that the Bratunac Brigade as it would be formed would draw from this geographical region its manpower, its resources, in order to have a significant number or an adequate number of soldiers in order to form its brigade and its battalions. Might that -- might I be in the same -- on the same wavelength with you on that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. In that respect, I mean, I believe I discussed that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could you point to us on the map where the zone of defence would be of the Bratunac Brigade as we all know it to have been for all those years, for 1992, 1993, 1994, 1995. And again we're referring to P369.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. Vague. That, it's Mr. Butler has already testified, that 1992 to 1995 constantly changed. I don't think Mr. Karnavas wants to hear all of that. I think I know what he wants and that's not a problem. If he can be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with this objection, Mr. Karnavas. You have to be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I was expecting the answer from the witness. It was a question designed to provoke the witness into saying I can't do that and I was going to walk him through. There are many different ways of cross-examining, but very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992 when it was initially formed, the Bratunac Brigade, where would the zone of operation would have been? Can you look at the map and give us a general description, and I know that things change. We've got the safe zones being created, but initially -- at least when this map was formed, where would their zone of operation have been?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I trust you're referring to where their defence line was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you read my mind, because that's within the zone of operation, but thank you. See, we're connecting now. Yes.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. You want the defence line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The defence line. And since we're referring to a map, and it's P369, if you could, and being a military man, give us sort of like coordinates, so we have it on record, we know east, west, south, north, those sorts of things. You don't have to give us the trig points, but if you want to, go for it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very roughly speaking, and it did change over time, just to orient, this is Bratunac. This is approximately, roughly, I think every 2 kilometres here for each grid square, so roughly about 6 kilometres to the west of the road you have what's known as the Kravica village complex. There are a couple of other key features to the south which would include the Sase mine complex up here in this area. And roughly speaking, in November 1992 the defence lines were very compressed at that point. From this region, it basically encompassed the large Bosnian Serb village complex of Kravica, Bratunac, and the Sase mine facilities up here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record you've moved your pointer --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Essentially from the Drina river, although it wasn't a cohesive defence, because it didn't have constant manning, but the main defensive positions were around the Serbian villages of Kravica, the Bosnian Serb villages, down the road toward the town of Bratunac. And then towards the south to encompass the Sase mine area. And that's my understanding roughly. And the big change in that of course occurred in early January 1993 when the Kravica village complex was taken by the Bosnian Muslims and that created a significant shortening of the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you read my next question. If you could show us what that line would have been. In other words, after the loss of territory or the gain of territory by the Muslim armed forces.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe at that time, and again I refer back to the Bratunac war history for the detailed specifics of that. It would have been almost -- at that time they lost the Kravica village complex, they were also pushed off the Sase mine complex. So by January of 1993, the defence lines were very much incorporated simply around holding the town of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So they had lost that much territory. Now, at some point -- and when you say the Kravica, we're talking about the massacre at the village over there, right, I think it was the Orthodox Christmas?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, we're talking about the Orthodox Christmas attack. I think it's January 6th --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 6th, 7th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Correct. Now, at some point, the VRS was able to gain territory and then we have a period of relative calm as far as where the lines are drawn. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The VRS, as part of their larger counter-offensive, starting in this area roughly late February or early March regains almost all of this territory and is compressing the OG8 and the Bosnian Muslim armed forces into the area of Srebrenica. And of course that was the genesis of the creation of the safe area. And once the borders of that were loosely defined, at that point in time things remained on a more static footage, at least with respect to that particular part of the Bratunac Brigade's lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And then finally, were there -- we're now here at this static period. What were the lines immediately prior to the attack on Srebrenica for the Bratunac Brigade, the defence lines, the zone of defence?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The defence lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 3rd Battalion roughly from the Pribicevac area along this series of ridges here to roughly Kos Mountain. From Kos, the 2nd Battalion were crossed over and had responsibility for both the east side and the west side of the Bratunac to Potocari highway. Further up the road in the area known as - and I want to pronounce it correctly - Magasici. Along the outer rim, the northern rim of the Srebrenica border, you had the 1st Infantry Battalion. And then from Kajici area, you had the 4th Infantry Battalion which ran out again towards the northern side of the rim of the enclave. This is the area, in the Ravni Buljin area here, where we discussed the issue of where the gap was. And then you started seeing units of the Milici Brigade on this ridge and in this area right here --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please, when you say ridge area, just for the record -- just so we have a notation.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In July of 1995, it would be in this very -- they establish a command post in the village of Brazinski [phoen] and on this ridge here, you'll see a note that says Ravni Buljin. And up on the ridge just to the west of it, they established defence lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll slow down a little bit. It would seem at least from what you're pointing at the defensive lines of the Milici Brigade at that period of time were in this marked area on this map that is attributed back as early as 1992 as the zone of responsibility for the Bratunac Brigade. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So we have at least by your estimation some units in that zone. Now, could we -- since that is part of their defence zone and since we have this map which would reflect not only the Bratunac Brigade defence, defence line or zone of operation, but also in the larger sense, the zone of responsibility in your context, might we conclude that the Milici's zone of responsibility in your context would be overlapping somewhat into this area, given that their zone of defence is already in there?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The Milici Brigade was directed to put a unit in there to try and plug that hole and in fact, did so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But does your zone of responsibility in your sense, would it not, if we use military logic, extend into that designated area, which you hold to be the zone of responsibility for the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we do have as somewhat similar as a Venn diagram one zone of responsibility superimposed on to another?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, I mean the most accurate way to put it is you have one unit operating in the zone of another. Now, whether zones changed or not, again as a component of my analysis, it didn't appear to be relevant at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you think it's relevant now?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to my understanding of the criminal acts that had occurred and the responsibility of Colonel Blagojevic, up until 15 July when there's an order that specifically indicates he takes command of that, I don't think it's relevant before that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe it's because I didn't get much sleep last night, you know the fog of war from last night. But my question is: Do you think it's relevant for this trial right now, for the period that we're discussing, not for that period back then. Do you think it would have been relevant for you to know, since you appear to at least acknowledge that the Milici Brigade is operating -- has a defence line within the designated zone of responsibility, which you attribute to the Bratunac Brigade. So my question is: Do you think it would be relevant to know whether the Milici Brigade's zone of responsibility is superimposed, goes into, part of the zone of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade, as designated on this map which you are relying on? Do you think it's relevant? Yes, no, I'll even take a maybe.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe it is, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Fair enough. What about the Skelani Brigade, where are they located, the battalion?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, if I can orient to the map, this is Srebrenica. This is Zeleni Jadar. This is the designated zone for the Skelani Separate Battalion, however their forces for the most part, as it was a rather small unit, were in July of 1995 ran up the road. And then at the intersection of Zeleni Jadar down towards the Jasenova area where they linked up with the Milici Brigade. So in this respect they had a rather small zone, and again some of it may very well have encroached into the zone identified as the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or maybe the accurate phrase is defence line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Because you threw me off there, and I don't want to discriminate the Milici Brigade, they only have a defence line and Skelani Battalion has the zone. So you're saying that their defence line -- are you saying might or did, in fact, go into the zone of responsibility, as you know it to be, of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it did go into the zone once the UN checkpoint at OP Echo was taken. So I believe they moved up at that point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You corrected yourself when you said they had a line of defence. Did they also have a zone of responsibility in addition to the line of defence?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As indicated in this map, there is a partial boundary. That is all the information that I have with respect to that battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But this map is with respect to what was -- I mean, if we are to accept the dates that it was drawn in 1992 to 1993, and I think we're pretty solid on that, you've indicated that things have changed, both on the battlefield but also with the development of the Drina Corps. In 1995, did the situation change and do you know how on the ground, geographically speaking?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I don't have any information from the Skelani Battalion which would lead me to have information one way or another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the answer to my question is you don't know?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So they very well could be operating like the Milici Brigade well into, or somewhat into this designated zone of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I believe that is the case.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel slow down a bit and perhaps speak into the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The fact that you don't know, is that again because you thought it was unimportant?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. With respect to, as I've indicated, the Bratunac Brigade records do not indicate a change and I do not have documents from Skelani that would allow me to research that from their point of view. So I just don't have the data is, I believe, the answer to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So putting it slightly differently, you did make efforts, you did make efforts to try to figure out to what extent the Skelani Battalion was operating within the zone of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade as you have designated to be, based on this map?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made efforts to understand what the Skelani Battalion was doing in July of 1995 with respect to laying it on this map, no. But with respect to the operation, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But -- well, before July 1995, before the attack, did you make any efforts, sir, to try to find out how or where the Skelani Battalion was located and whether they were operating within -- to what extent, I should say, within the zone of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Might I conclude that perhaps those efforts weren't made because you didn't think it was a significant or a relevant issue in this case?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, was that based on a -- was that a military -- from a military standpoint or from a legal standpoint? And I do understand that you're not a lawyer, but you talked about crimes that occurred in 1995, so I assume that you have some general gist of what this case is all about as far as the legal nature is concerned.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given the fact that -- and again, I think I can combine the two on this one, given the fact that we are dealing with the issue of superior command responsibility and given the fact that most of the information that I have, one, on the basis of JNA rules, and two, on the basis of VRS documents, are very clear with respect to the issues of subordination and how they're done within the units, of military units. Again as I note, I didn't see it as a relevant issue, because to my knowledge where the structure of the indictment on the issues of superior responsibility reflect those units with respect to those under the command or control of the accused. So that is the light in which I looked at it with respect to the relevancy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I understand you correctly, it is at least your perception or your understanding that if certain criminal acts occur in this area that you attribute as a zone of responsibility for the Bratunac Brigade, and if those acts, those criminal acts, are done by units other than the Bratunac Brigade, albeit in their zone of responsibility, the Bratunac Brigade is not responsible?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In respect to the issue of command, yes. In respect to the issue of superior responsibility, I believe that I would default back to the articles 21 and 22 of the SFRY rules of the application of the law of land warfare, which broaden it out to the context that for the issue of superior responsibility, if an officer who finds out in his units or in other units. So in a technical issue of command, no. In the broader issue of superior responsibility, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I guess, given your understanding of the law and through the use of your military logic, you thought on your own that it was unimportant to see whether this map was correct or not, because I would assume that it would not make military logic to have two, possibly three, zones of responsibility in the same area? In other words, the same area, you have three different -- or two brigades and one battalion sharing it as a zone of their responsibility. That would not make military logic, would it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm confused by your question. Let me just break it down for a second here, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'm rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is based on your understanding of the law as you indicated and your reliance on it, that you decided that it was unimportant to determine where the battalion -- the Milici Battalion -- Milici Brigade and the Skelani Battalion were operating within the zone of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade. That question was unimportant to you. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could just clarify. Are we speaking of law in terms of the JNA rules or international law or the law of the indictment? There's been a lot of potential law being mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Based --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you have to rephrase it because it's still difficult for us to understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll break it down. Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were given a task to analyse and synthesise the information available to you with respect to what exactly happened in Srebrenica during the time in question. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And part of that analysis and synthesis was to determine who should be held responsible for and, as a result, who should be prosecuted for the crimes that occurred in and around Srebrenica back in July 1995. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a broader sense, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In a broader sense. Well, that was basically the whole sense of the investigation that was done by the Office of the Prosecution, to bring to justice those who would be responsible. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, part of your analysis in trying to figure out how the JNA worked -- the VRS worked was to go to their rules and regulations as well as the legislation that they had adopted specifically as it related to the military and its behaviour. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in doing so, you came across legislation which we -- I think we can all agree meets the standard that is expected under international law.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The standard of what, sir?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the standard of behaviour for soldiers in the field.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I believe those regulations are in compliance with the greater body of laws of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And if I understand your answers earlier, you've indicated -- you know, you use the terms "command and control," and that term would be military, would it not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you made references to command responsibility or superior responsibility, and that concept is part military but also an aspect of it with respect to -- in a legal sense. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, in order to understand whether a commander is responsible, one of the things you need to look at is the command and control aspect. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And based on that, you would then try to determine whether you could fix responsibility on a commander based on his actions or his failures to act, given the circumstances. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in part of your analysis and synthesis you have indicated that the Bratunac Brigade had a zone of responsibility, have you not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that zone of responsibility you have indicated, though you have not been able to show us anywhere in the rules where that concept exists with respect to brigades specifically --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, to the argumentative nature of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase. I'll rephrase. Not a problem. Not a problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, now have determined that the zone of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade is based on some documents and not grounded in the regulations or the rules as such. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And in part -- in making that assessment, that the Bratunac Brigade had a zone of responsibility, you're relying on certain documents, such as this map. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A map that you determined was created by Colonel Zivanovic back at the end of 1992, perhaps as early -- at the beginning of 1993. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've also indicated that from 1992 or towards the -- from 1992 to 1995 when Srebrenica is attacked, the situation is, to use your term, is fluid or was fluid for a certain period of time. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: From -- with respect to the Drina Corps, from November 1992 to May of 1993, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you use the term "fluid," you meant with respect to the borders, between the RS and the Muslim-held territory. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. What I mean fluid is the various military operations and defence lines that occurred with respect to Bratunac, Skelani, and the general area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And it was during this period in 1993 when in this area, if we look at this map which purports to reflect the zone of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade, there is the creation of the safe area of Srebrenica. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And so that might we say is somewhat of a significant development with respect to the lay of the land as it is reflected on this particular map.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We've also indicated that at some point there was a stablisation between the VRS and the 28th Division which occurred as a result of the UN coming in, establishing the safe zone, separating in essence the two armies, the VRS and the 2nd Corps -- or unit of the 2nd Corps, which was the 28th Division, located in and armed within the enclave of Srebrenica. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now -- and at some point during that stabilisation process -- I should say at some point after the establishment of this map we also know that we have one brigade being formed, which is the Milici Brigade and also we have some development -- some further development in the establishment of the Skelani Battalion. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And we do know, at least from your testimony, that both the brigade and the battalion were operating in what purports to be from this map the zone of responsibility attributed to the Bratunac Brigade. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- and it would seem to me -- well, it would seem through use of military logic that if the Bratunac Brigade has a line of defence which is within the context of a zone of operation as well as, as well as, a zone of responsibility encompassing a fairly large geographical region, that if we use that logic, at least for the Milici Brigade, we would also have to conclude, would we not, that the Milici Brigade also has a zone of responsibility in addition to its line of defence, which is part of its zone of operation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would conclude that the Milici Brigade has a zone of responsibility and that they are operating in it, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And if they're operating, if the Milici Brigade is operating within its zone of responsibility, axiomatically, we could conclude that if they are within this designated area which you purport to the zone of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade, their zone of responsibility would be inside this part of the map that is highlighted as a zone of responsibility for the Bratunac Brigade. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So now we have two zones of responsibility in this area that this map which was drafted in 1992 purports to be the zone - and I should add the word sole zone - of responsibility for the Bratunac Brigade. I'm taking a bit of a liberty, because I don't see any -- when it says zone of responsibility, it doesn't say, and others.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. In that respect, yes, sir, okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And of course would you -- and I'm asking you to go out on a limb on this one, but down here we have the Skelani Battalion. Do they have a zone of responsibility in the sense as you have described what a zone of responsibility is for a brigade, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say exactly. However, given that it was the practice, I think it would be fair to conclude that they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So -- again, using military logic, if they too have a zone and if they too are operating within this designated area, which you purport to be the zone of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade, the Skelani Battalion's zone of responsibility would also be inclusive, inclusive, into this section of the map where they're located and operating. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, again, sir, their defence lines would be. Whether that results in a formal changing of a zone of responsibility, I don't know the answer to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I skipped a beat, because I covered that with the Milici. So let me go back, throw that one in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that subject has been gone into four or five times. I don't think it takes us anywhere to go through it six times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I want a very clear record on this one and it's only a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we indicated that -- initially I indicated that you have a line of defence which is part of a zone of operation, which you have told us is within a zone of responsibility. And the answers were yes, yes, yes. So then we concluded, did we not, through military logic, of course, that the same would apply to the Milici Brigade. So then I asked you about the battalion, because you see now there is a distinction between brigade and battalion. So my question now is: If we are using military logic, if their line of defence is inside where the Bratunac Brigade's zone of responsibility is, according to this map, and if their line of defence would be inclusive within their zone of responsibility which you believe they must have, then it stands to follow, and this one we can use Aristotelian logic, we don't even need to use military logic. It would stand to reason, would it not, that their zone of responsibility would be within this area which you have designated as the zone of responsibility for the Bratunac Brigade. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that that's a technically accurate logic trail. And perhaps the best way to explain it is to put it in a broader context. During the course of the war, many battalions from many formations were pulled from their parent units and sent to man defence lines in the zones of responsibilities of other brigades. When they manned those defence lines, clearly they are given a responsibility for the terrain in front of them and other military responsibilities. I don't believe that the next step in that logic train is that you can then conclude that the parent unit no longer -- not the parent unit, the unit whose zone they are operating in is suddenly absolved of all broader responsibility. These lines are designated by the superior command, not by the brigades themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I haven't asked a question yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: At this point I don't understand the further relevance of this. We don't have any crime scenes that I'm aware in this area of Milici/Bratunac that's being spoken of. It's Mr. Karnavas's duty to put his position to Mr. Butler on this point so we can find out where he's going. I think he's going there, but at this point it seems to be circular.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I haven't asked a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We have already spent a lot of time on that issue and at least the witness answered the question twice. I think that's the most we can get.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In my defence, Your Honour, I was moving on. I hadn't formed a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, move on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I was pre-emptively struck.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: These are unnecessary comments, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, if Mr. Karnavas has a point with this zone of responsibility thing, he's required to make it to Mr. Butler so that Mr. Butler can now explain it so we don't have to bring Mr. Butler back from the United States to explain the point Mr. Karnavas is getting to. I still don't understand the point because the crime scenes are in Bratunac, they're in Potocari, they're in Kravica, they're in Konjevic Polje. None of these areas have we really talked about yet, and he has a duty to get to his point. I think he's going to, he usually does. But that is the basis of my objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I wasn't aware that I need to send a telegram to the Prosecution. In any event, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The law requires him to, Your Honour. It is a British rule, but it's designed so that the person being cross-examined can explain the point that the person is trying to make. I don't remember the rule number, but I can get it for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, anyway, Mr. Karnavas, please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. When are we breaking, Your Honour, just to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll break at 12.00 sharp. But if you need we could have an early break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I would prefer at this point, Your Honour, because I have a slight migraine and if we could take a break and let me regroup for the final segment for today and we can come back earlier, of course. I'm not trying to delay. I'm willing to go forward, but I would appreciate if we could break and not chop up my next segment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I think this request is reasonable and we are very flexible and we'll resume at 20 past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. Your next segment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we get to that, Your Honour, yesterday I misspoke when I mentioned that the brigade rules were D83. In fact, they are -- they were introduced as D82 for identification purposes. So if the record could reflect that and be corrected, we could most appreciate it and I apologise to -- for that error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Butler, if we could pick up where we left off last night where my interests had been piqued a little bit. Now, yesterday as I understand it, you made this observation with respect to what the Trial Chamber knows about large numbers of troops from the Bratunac Brigade being in Potocari. Do you recall making a statement to that effect?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the exact phrase was significant. I didn't quantify large.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Significant. Well, significant, though, in a sense does mean many, does it not, as opposed to few?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It also means in another sense a broader cross-section of the unit. So it has, for me, two meanings in that respect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that based on military logic or is that based on the Webster's dictionary on the English language?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on how I've always used the phrase, sir, sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, if we could look at your narrative, which I believe has been marked for identification purposes as P358, if you could just get it out handy first. Just have it handy there. And I'm going to be referring to pages 82 and -- I'm sorry, 42 and 44. And we do have an extra copy for the ELMO in the event we failed to provide sufficient numbers of copies. Now, just get it open --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which pages, sir?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's page 42 to start with. This way you can follow along. Now, before I ask you the pertinent questions, with respect to this document, a little foundation. I take it that in doing your narrative you did, in fact, include those whom you believed were in Potocari on the days in question. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I did my narrative, I included the names of key individuals who were identified at the time by either witnesses or by video evidence who were noted in Potocari on either 12 or 13 July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you use the words "key individuals," please explain, what do you mean by key?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this respect, key individuals, and given that the context of the very first piece of this, all we really had was the video and identifications that we're making off the video. So in this regard, I did not include everybody and I'm aware the investigation has identified a much more significant number of individuals from selections of these units, particularly, I believe, the 2nd Battalion who were in Potocari. So that is what this was limited to at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did the OTP identify these individuals prior to revising your narrative or subsequent to?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that a number of them were identified before I had revised my narrative, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it those who were identified prior to the revision of the narrative were included in the narrative?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I did not, because I understood that it was the intent that that witness-based material would be tendered through other means. So, again in keeping with my role of trying to focus on documents and intercepts as much as possible, I did not do that in that respect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That was a choice that you made or was the choice one that was made for you or was it a coordinated choice between you and the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was considered coordinated, but the trial team is well aware of my reluctance to use witness-based evidence as a component of my own analytical reports, particularly given the fact that witnesses may or may not testify here before the Trial Chamber. And of course they're subject to cross-examination. So in that respect, they're well aware of that practice that not only I, but most of the military analysts, have. And when they structure their exhibit lists, they do so knowing that some of this information will have to be brought in through witnesses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understood the answer to my question. My question was whether it was a decision that you made solely and independently. Was it one that you got your marching orders from the Prosecution, or was it one where you sat down and decided, okay, let's leave it with the names that you've already put in of key witnesses or the key members of the Bratunac Brigade and the others, let's deal with them through another means?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that respect, I believe it was a coordinated approach, because I just didn't want to remove anything that had been in the prior narrative and I knew there was additional information that would come in through witnesses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we're not talking about removing. We're talking about adding. So you could have added those names if you had chosen to. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could have added those names, but then again I'm unable to place considerable weight behind them unless the witness himself comes forward and testifies as such.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. When you say "weight," are you suggesting that simply because they were present they had -- you cannot make any sense of their mere presence, and therefore, unless you have something much more tangible, only then would you put that information into your report, into your narrative?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. With this respect what I mean is that as an analyst, I don't know this individual by sight. Some of them, obviously, I do, but most of them, of course, I will not. My making a conclusion that a particular witness has correctly identified a person is meaningless unless the witness himself testifies that that's the proper identification.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of all the people that you've listed in your report, in your narrative, the key members of the Bratunac Brigade, were they all interviewed by the Office of the Prosecution? Yes, no, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I expect that some were not. I mean, certainly everyone wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the answer is I don't know?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But closer to no, not everyone?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer is I don't know. I mean, certainly we didn't interview everyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And was that because of an inability to locate those witnesses or perhaps a shortage of funds of the OTP, shortage of time, resources, or just plain, for lack of a better term, disinterest?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how to answer this question in a short answer, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can go for one of your long ones. I don't care.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer changes over time. Certainly from the very beginning we were interested in interviewing the Bosnian Serb army or VRS officers. It was not until, to my knowledge, December of 1999 where the Office of the Prosecutor, working through summonses with the government of Srpska, was ever in a position to have these individuals available for interview. We had no mechanism, to my knowledge, prior to that to go out and find these individuals and have them show up at a location and be interviewed. Particularly with the first series of interviews, they went successfully with compliance, insomuch as they were senior officers, many were still serving in the VRS and the Republika Srpska made them available for interview. As we continued to develop the situation over time and over years, and we started getting down to the lower-level individuals in both the Zvornik and the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, a number of these people were being summonsed and not showing up for interviews or we were being informed that individuals were no longer in the territory. Certainly as we get into the latter years of the investigation, there will be other investigative priorities and budget constraints that didn't exist in the early years. So the answer tends to change over time as to why we did not get out and interview everybody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, given your answer that you just gave us, who among the folks that you summoned that you have included in your narrative as being from the Bratunac Brigade, which one of those were summoned and failed to appear at the appropriate time and place, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know offhand, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Which of them were you unable to locate, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those records are maintained up in -- with the investigation. I don't know the answer offhand, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which of them had left the area, the vicinity, where one would find them, that is the Bratunac/Srebrenica location. Which of them had left the vicinity?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, sir, while that information is available, I don't know it off the top of my head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You've indicated that you only included the key personnel. How many exactly did you include in your report, in your narrative?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That's a misstatement. He did not say he only included the key personnel. That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, feel free whenever you want to jump in and correct me. Mr. McCloskey shouldn't have to do that. You can do that, too. Now, if we look at -- I think I might be able to direct you to 5.11 and 5.12 on page 42 and then again, I believe, 5.21 and 5.22 on page 44.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could look at those relevant portions on page 42 and page 44, you might be able to give us a ballpark figure of the significant numbers you talked about.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to Mr. Zoran Kovacevic --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't know need to know specific names, just listen to the question. It's pretty fundamental.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this respect, one, two, and then I believe three, four, five, six, seven, eight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And the -- and forgive me, I don't mean it to sound in a pejorative sense, but in the Butler lexicon, would that be a significant number?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, the number eight is not a significant number unless you're talking of a population group of ten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In the context in which we're talking, to use another one of your phrases, and in your own lexicon, would eight be a significant number?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the broader context of the Bratunac Brigade, while the number eight would not be a significant number, I will again go back to some of these individuals are in leadership positions, which would increase their significance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're going to get to that.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: But numerically the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're going to go step by step. So let me direct you, please. So the answer is: Eight is not a significant number, but in your opinion these are key individuals. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them are, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Some of them are. And I take it that because some of them are "key individuals," you give that a significance?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And the reason you give it a significance because it is your belief, perhaps maybe even understanding, that because of their position, one, they must have been ordered to go there. Correct? That's one possibility.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a possibility, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two, because of their position, obviously they might or they must have or might have or would have, pick any three, brought with them subordinate members of their unit. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's a possibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's a possibility. And so given their position, you gave them -- you termed them to be key -- at least worthy enough, worthy enough, to be memorialised in your narrative. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to the initial version of the narrative, it was less memorialised, and everyone who we were properly able to identify at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly this list has expanded in numbers over the years of the investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Might I be able to pry out of you the exact number?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I've ever counted up the exact number with respect to identifications of numbers of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, again, I mean I have to fall back on your lexicon. You said significant. Obviously there must be a threshold where you go from not significant, almost significant, to significant. Where is the threshold? Where is that line? What number do we get to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection to vagueness. Significant to what? This is critical. There has been significance in terms of larger numbers to smaller numbers, which doesn't have much meaning for this case. There's tremendous kinds of significance. So I don't know what the question means and I don't think there's any way Mr. Butler -- Mr. Butler may guess or Mr. Butler may have his opinion what he means, but without more specificity, it's very difficult to say what kind of significance he's talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, we also fail to see your point in asking these kind of questions. Would you please ask some questions around that key numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I don't mean to be disrespectful, but if I might respond. We've listened to a great deal of testimony on direct. Terms have been thrown out and obviously I was not permitted to object in a fashion and means in which I'm used to objecting, in keeping with the Court's ruling, which I respected although I must say I was having a hard time maintaining my equilibrium sitting here. So now that I have the opportunity to hear the gentleman use such words as "the Trial Chamber well knows" and uses "significant," these are buzz words. So now I'm trying to use his own words, because what I'm trying to demonstrate is part of his lexicon is gobbledygook. Part of his lexicon cannot be defined. So, in his own mind, when he says "significant," what is it? Because he may have a different meaning in his mind than the one that we may have. And I would like to know at what point does the number rise to the level where we can call it significant. Of course Mr. McCloskey has objected but we all know what we're talking about. Within, to quote Mr. Butler, "the broader context".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe that's not the problem of the numbers, maybe it's about, you know, those people are affiliated too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I didn't get that, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe that is the unit those numbers are affiliated to. Let us hear the witness. He will tell us about the using of the words of the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So help us out here a little bit here, Mr. Butler. When you use the word "significant," in the greater context of what was happening in Potocari on the morning or throughout the day of the 12th and 13th of July, 1995, how do you come up with this description of "significant"? Help us out. What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I can straighten that out very quickly, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to interviews that have been conducted by the Office of the Prosecution, we know, for example -- and I'll use this specifically, Zoran Kovacevic, the 4th Company commander indicated that his company with him was in Potocari, that they were directed by their battalion commander to come off of their defensive positions, move into Potocari, and in his interview later he says he met his battalion commander, or at that time it was acting commander and they were moved back to the wood line. We interviewed the battalion commander who acknowledges the presence of Zoran Kovacevic, although he notes that he didn't know that at the time. And in being shown pictures of individuals, he identifies out of a number of soldiers seen on that video groups of soldiers that correspond to -- and I believe he specifically identifies them as members of the 3rd Infantry Company of the 2nd Battalion. So in that context right there, there are at least the significant elements, in the case of the 4th Company, the full company of that battalion in Potocari. Going back to my narrative report, you have an identification of Zoran Milosavljevic who is the commander of the intervention platoon of that battalion. So you're now approaching the threshold where you have almost half the battalion is in Potocari on that day, during the morning and early afternoon hours. You have in other respects members of the 3rd Battalion identified that day, although in limited numbers. You have the assistant commander for rear services, Major Trisic, who in an interview with the OTP acknowledged that he was there that day with the rear services unit because they had been directed to provide bread to the Bosnian Muslim people in Potocari. You have the assistant commander for security and intelligence, Momir Nikolic. So I mean, that in my mind is the threshold of significant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you say half of a battalion was there. That is your understanding and belief that half of the battalion, half of the 4th Battalion was in Potocari on that day.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. Half of the 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 2nd Battalion --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 4th Company, the 3rd Company --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The entire companies were there?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the company commander of the 4th Company, his entire company was there. According to the video footage, it is my belief that the bulk of the 3rd Company, given the fact that a company in that time frame numbered between 50 and 60 people, I believe I can say the bulk of them were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say the bulk of them --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like I say, I have not counted the actual numbers of soldiers who walked by, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can counsel and the witness please pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, numerically, give us a figure. I mean, you seem to have a ballpark understanding of what portions of which units were there, the implication being that they were there doing something. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were there doing something. I would say if you're asking for a ballpark figure, perhaps 90 to 120-ish. I think that's a low-end figure, but I want to be conservative on this one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's your understanding that they were there under orders?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic, the company commander, said that he was there under orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did his commander say?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: His commander said that he had no knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which means that he would not have been under orders?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that there's a conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, one is saying, I know -- you see, you tend to -- when it benefits the Prosecutor -- I understand you're a member of their team, you like it --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, this is very argumentative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So his commander denies giving him any orders. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which of the two do you tend to believe, that he was or he was not given orders?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I believe that both of them are probably misrepresenting certain aspects of their interviews.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that because they're members of the VRS and you would expect all of them to just lie?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, that is uncalled for and if this starts up again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He said "misrepresentations," he's jumping to a conclusion. What is the basis for him stating that both are misrepresenting the truth

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, This is a serious subject. Mr. Karnavas has repeatedly accused me personally of vilifying Serbs. This has affected my reputation in this community. I can handle that. We don't need this to be connected to Mr. Butler, without some proof that he is a racist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do not argue with each other in this courtroom, Mr. Karnavas. I think I have warned you many times. Just get to your question to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your basis, other than the fact that they are members of the VRS, what is your basis in believing that both of them are misrepresenting the truth?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. There has been no foundation. He said other than the VRS, that is not a fact. That's not proven, and that's just his addition. And I'm sorry to objecting but this is something I will not stand for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we are not going to discuss this issue. Mr. Karnavas, just ask that simple and plain question. I think that question is relevant, but do not unnecessarily offend anybody in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's no -- no one's trying to offend anyone. They are members of the VRS. That is a fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If it is a fact, everyone knows it. There's no need for you to stress it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the basis for you stating or believing that they're both misrepresenting the truth?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let's just keep it narrowed down to the specific issue of 12 July, if we shall. I mean -- because when I said misrepresenting the truth on their entire interviews, it's the entirety of the interview. With respect to 12 July, the video evidence that we have tends to corroborate the issue that the commander of the 4th Battalion -- I'm sorry, the commander of the 4th Company of the 2nd Battalion was in Potocari at the time. The identification by that company commander that he received orders from his battalion commander personally tends to correspond with the known fact that the local battalions or certainly the companies did not have adequate means of radio communications, and that orders would have to be passed either over the radio telephone or in person. So in this respect, I mean I believe that Zoran Kovacevic's account of the events that put him in Potocari is probably more accurate in the context of other information I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're saying the other gentleman, his commander is lying?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe he's being untruthful. I don't think he's being fully candid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that point?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is that he did not order those men over there?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he was questioned on that issue -- when he was questioned on that issue, he said it was possible they were ordered by the deputy commander of the battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: He stated that he did not order them. I'm not talking about the deputy commander, I'm talking about him. Right?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you seem to be implying that this man is lying about that.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am saying that I don't believe he is fully truthful with that respect, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course if you had believed him versus the other, it might not be so rosy for the Prosecutor, would it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, this is precisely why I don't include this information in my reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you included the name, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only included the name because it's footnoted to a piece of video evidence. This name was included in my initial version of the narrative long before we had the opportunity to interview this individual.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you interview other members, as many as you could, to tell which of the two were telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did interview other members, but I believe in this context those are the only two individuals with respect to that issue that were interviewed. I don't believe the investigation has gone out and attempted to talk to other soldiers further down the line on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the deputy commander, since that was a possibility?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I checked that, and his name -- we don't have an interview from him. So I don't know whether he has been summoned for investigation -- for interview or not. So I don't know the answer to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But nonetheless you made a conclusion that one is telling the truth and one is not telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. You've asked me for that conclusion and I've made it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course. And now of course the person who told the truth according to you, if he had gone there on his own without orders and he's seen on video, might he be somewhat fearful that he could end up at The Hague or be prosecuted because there he is on video and therefore would have a reason to perhaps fabricate that he was there on orders by his commander. Might that be a possibility within the greater context of what is happening on that day and then later on and over here?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We can move on to another topic. If we could now draw your attention to P543, which is the preparatory order that was drafted by the Drina Corps for July 2, 1995. I thought we could discuss that a little bit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: P543, I believe that's the one I have here. It's the Drina Corps July 2, preparatory order, the order for active combat activities. I think you know what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what you're talking about, but that's a higher number than I associated it with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I might be wrong, but I have it at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We have an additional one for the ELMO, so you don't have to --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll need it, sir, apparently I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we thought ahead. I take it that over the years you've had a chance to look at this and analyse it quite a bit, have you not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I'm sorry, this is the actual order. This is not the preparatory order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe I misspoke. The order for Krivaja 95. Now, you've had a chance to look at this, have you not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I'm familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I know you touched on this a little bit, but I would like to focus your attention on the first paragraph, if you could, at least the first portion of the first paragraph number 1 where -- first why don't you read it to yourself and then maybe perhaps we could -- real quickly and then we could focus in on it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in reading this paragraph it seems to be stating that the VRS is expecting an attack from the Muslim army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It notes not only are they expecting, but in the broader context they are still dealing with historical attacks, so yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say "historical attacks," what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I think I've pointed out in my narrative, consistent with the ABiH 2 Corps offensive, or the Sarajevo offensive, the 28th Division was instructed to carry out a series of attacks out of the enclave, in order to keep forces tied down. So that's what I mean, in this context they had already received attacks and were anticipating more of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I take it, just to stay on that, I take it that if those folks from the 28th Division that were going and killing innocent Serbs in their villages and committing war crimes, then the commanders all the way up to the height of the BiH government in Sarajevo would have been responsible for those atrocities?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this respect, and I know that there's a related case to this going on or shortly going on, but certainly if they were killing civilians in that context as opposed to straight military activities, there should be a chain of accountability, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which would go all the way to the top of -- it would have gone all the way to the top of Alija Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Presumably, yes, sir. He, as the president, and again my knowledge of the ABiH military structure is not as detailed, but as the president, if he's functioning as the supreme commander, it would be a responsibility that would ultimately would rest at his lap.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So -- but overall, correct me if I'm wrong, and you probably know better than I do, by this period of the events that are happening in Bosnia in general, the Muslim and Croatian armies are becoming stronger and stronger. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact, as I understand it, and you've indicated this, the Muslim army, numerically speaking at least, numerically speaking was much larger than the VRS?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it would appear, and I think you've touched on this, that one of the objectives -- I guess by serendipity by having these enclaves there, allowed the 28th Division, hiding under the protection of the UN, to go into these attacks, occasional attacks, thus requiring the VRS, in particular the Drina, the Drina Corps, to more or less have permanent defensive lines. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by doing so, at least they could pin down almost an entire corps and perhaps more just for that purpose. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In context with the Zepa and Gorazde safe areas, they did in fact pin down almost all of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course, if there was something happening in the Sarajevo area that the Muslim army wanted to engage in an attack, they could easily, and they would I believe, have the 28th Division mount a little attack into the VRS territory, the area over there, thus engaging the Drina Corps so as to make sure that no reinforcements could get to the Sarajevo area, thus permitting the Muslims to have the advantage. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And in fact that was the practice and the goal of -- the goal that was behind it, the prevent the VRS and specifically the Drina Corps from being able to send sizeable reinforcements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would appear from this particular section that they're almost forecasting that there is imminent threat ahead of us?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that they expect a two-frontal attack at some point?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir -- or at least -- yeah, as part of an operation to cut the corps in half, so yes, sir, in conjunction with the other forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just to make sure that I'm on the right wavelength, what do I mean by that? Can you explain to me what I just meant when I said two-frontal attack. I'm not asking you to be clairvoyant.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe what you're getting to is the situation where military forces operating out of Zepa and Srebrenica, moving in one direction towards the larger line of the BiH and the ABiH 2 Corps forces moving out in the other direction towards those, in effect a movement to pinch or cut the corps in half.
