And the practical aspect of that is it looked very much like the military events that were occurring on 14 and 15 July is probably the best way in context to say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if that were to occur, I guess, and they were able to as the Muslim forces would have been going in their various directions, they would have been cleansing the area, or at least pushing the Serb population out of that area, thus expanding their territory which would have been Muslim-held. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the purpose of had it been their intent to actually link up the lines and hold territory, that that would have been in effect what they did in 1992 and early 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And so it would appear, would it not that this Krivaja 95, when it was drafted and in the way it was drafted and its purpose was in essence to stage, to mount, a pre-emptive strike. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As its written, I believe that's the language that they used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yeah. It's like President George Bush thinking that Iraq has chemical weapons, he pre-emptively strikes to make sure nothing happens. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, that comment is totally irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I was trying to put it into the context --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Don't try that. Don't try that. I don't want these proceedings more complicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I'm not trying to complicate the situation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I guess what I'm trying to get through that example and perhaps it wasn't artfully stated, it would seem to me that pre-emptively striking, especially when you believe you are going to be attacked, and secondly when you are at a disadvantage, is militarily correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is certainly a sound military strategy, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So we can agree at least that the attack on Srebrenica, pre-emptive as it may have been, was, at least in the mind of the VRS, which you seem to be confirming at least on what was happening on the grounds, a means of avoiding an attack that was about to happen?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a perspective that they followed and it's a valid one. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And had they not been on the offensive at one point, they would have found themselves on the defensive. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in fact, they were on the defensive for the period up to that operation. But again, given the context of the larger events that occur later that July and in August, the situation for as bad as it was for the VRS probably would have been even worse, had they not have launched this operation. They would have not been able to pull any of the manpower out of the Drina Corps at that time. So certainly they understood the ramifications, the senior planners of the VRS, when they put this together and what it would mean and it did have that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just to add another piece to the puzzle, as I understand it in addition to the Muslim army being numerically larger or having the advantage, at around this time also or building up to this time, quite a bit of weapons and military hardware was coming into their position from various foreign entities. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand that particularly with respect to Srebrenica that there were weapons being smuggled in, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And just as an aside, but perhaps it might be relevant, we know that the 28th Division in Srebrenica was relatively large, at least numerically speaking, and when I say "large," I'm giving it the figure of somewhere between five to six, maybe even larger, maybe even slightly smaller. But 5 to 6.000 soldiers. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That number is consistent with numbers that I've seen. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there Mujahedin working in Srebrenica at the time, if you are aware of that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not believe we have any evidence that says that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But Mujahedin were operating in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and we're talking about foreign fighters coming in and assisting the Muslim army. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, can you give us an estimation how large the Muslim army was on the other side where the Zvornik Brigade was located, in other words, from the Tuzla area.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can give you a rough context insomuch as they were facing the 24th Infantry Division, which had a number of brigades. I know we have some of the documents, but I have not researched that in detail. But without using something from my lexicon, I can say they were significantly outnumbered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And what about resource-wise, did they have -- numbers is one thing, but they obviously need weapons. So weapon-wise, how were they in that department?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in a broader context, they also had less weaponry than the VRS did. However, by early 1995, certainly with respect to weapons that were coming into Tuzla, and in many respects those being forwarded to the units of the 2nd Corps, their ability with respect to the VRS with weapons was improving. I'm not sure that it ever reaches parity, but certainly with respect to the overall VRS it was improving on a weekly basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were they receiving these resources, this military hardware -- or I should say were they not receiving this military hardware or some of it from foreign entities that were assisting in smuggling into their territory?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I understand that there were a number of foreign parties that were involved in that practice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you give us the names of some of those foreign parties.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in this respect, my source of information for this would be the book written by Mr. Cees Wiebes, since I have no firsthand knowledge of this. However, he indicates in his book that the United States was one of the parties which, in fact, supplied weapons to ABiH 2 Corps, not specifically but to the Bosnian Muslim government beginning in January of 1995 through a series of supposedly clandestine flights to Tuzla airfield where these weapons were offloaded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then some of those weapons were being flown in to Srebrenica, which was a safe zone protected by the United Nations. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, it is my understanding from both the book by Mr. Wiebes and the UN report, that on select helicopter flights, they were smuggling weapons and other military equipment into Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the way, this gentleman in his book, that is the one that's written on intelligence -- his title escapes me, but I believe it's intelligence --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I know which one you're talking about. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it derives from -- he's a Dutch fellow that's in Amsterdam I believe and he derives a lot of his material from the report on Srebrenica that was done by the Dutch government. Is that correct? And other resources as well.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I believe it is. It is well documented there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- and you are aware, just to get back to the flights into Srebrenica, that there was some witnesses who testified that there were downing of at least one helicopter?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know from the VRS documents that the Drina Corps made an active attempt to bring down helicopters that were flying in and I understand that at least one was taken down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we know that there was a region known as the Bandera triangle in the Srebrenica safe area, do we not, you've heard of that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I believe I discussed that area in my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was an area that was within the enclave where the UN were supposed to protect and monitor to make sure that it was demilitarised, was it not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was -- the practical reality was that the 28th Infantry Division forces would not permit the UN to freely move in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, it made sure they had no or as little access as possible to that area. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact you know, as we all know from the testimony that has come before this Court, that at some point the members of the 28th Division held hostage the DutchBat for two or three or four days, I believe, because they dared to do their UN duties and venture into that area where presumably illegal activity, at least under the UN mandate, was occurring, that is, storing weapons. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. In respect to they did hold members of Dutch Battalion hostage. I'm not sure of all of the other things. I assume the answer would be yes, but I don't know for a fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, getting back to this order, if we were to look at -- does this order mandate a role for the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it does specifically, and I'll come to the paragraph here. I believe it's on page 4 of the English language translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We're not going to get to it just yet.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this order is rather specific as to who is going to be involved. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Insomuch as --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The units.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The units, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it gives them some guidance as to the level of their involvement. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is there anything in this order with respect to potential capture of war prisoners?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And where might we find that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be in paragraph 10, which is page 7 of the English language translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And if we could -- if you could be so kind, you're pretty handy with that ELMO there. All right. Now, what does it say about war prisoners.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The security organs -- I'm sorry, the first one. "Security organs and military police will indicate the areas for gathering and securing prisoners of war and war booty."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me stop you right there. So this order gives the task to the security organ. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the military police, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is that the security organ of the Drina Corps or is it the security organ of the various units that are going to be engaged in this operation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this respect, I would read this as the security organs, it says plural, and military police. So there are two ways to look at it. I mean, my initial view is that it is a specified task to all of the units of the Drina Corps in this case. So security organs and military police will indicate the areas. I mean, again, because it's plural, I believe that this is to all of the units that are involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what does -- does that mean that it would be up to the security organ to decide and have the ultimate say-so?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I don't believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What exactly does that mean, at least to your understanding?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this respect what it means is that the commander is designating the security organs and military police as a function will indicate these areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. For instance, as an example, during the attack on Srebrenica if, for instance, the Bratunac Brigade were to come up with -- capture any prisoners of war, they would be the responsibility of the commander of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And not the security organ of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the commander designates that responsibility to the security organ, then it would become their responsibility, yes, sir, in that respect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's a delegation of duty but not of authority or responsibility?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a delegation of authority, not of responsibility yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think we can all agree that a commander can never delegate his responsibility?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He's the commander and that's it. Okay. Now -- so your understanding is that it's the security organs, plural. What role does the security organ of the Drina Corps play vis-a-vis the security organs of the various battalions or units that are involved in this operation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this respect, and again I don't have the full answer to this, so in this respect what I believe the guidance is to provide technical assistance or the professional support to the subordinate security branches, which might include such functions as detailing the availability or lack of availability of the corps military police battalion to engage in such operations. It might engage in identifying a corps-designated site, which all of the brigades will be required to forward their prisoners to. It might designate those things within its purview that would be of the general use and direction for the entire corps. So those the types of functions that come to mind, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could just move to the section with respect to the tasks that are ordered of the Bratunac Brigade. And again, I'm going to be asking you to comment on their involvement in the greater context of the attack. If you could put it into that greater context, as I think you tend to do anyway, but just in case I'm not clear. Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. You want it on the ELMO, sir?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could put it on the ELMO and direct our attentions so just for the record, so we have it, again we're referring to P543/A --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The Bratunac Brigade order?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. The section -- we're going to get to that order, too. So keep that handy. The section within this order, 2 July 1995, what mission is given to the Bratunac Brigade. That's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be page 4 of the English language.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you've read this, and I take it you studied it, analysed it, and probably synthesised it in the greater context of this entire order. So concretely and as clearly as possible, could you tell us what exactly is going to be the role of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As envisioned by the Drina Corps, the Bratunac Brigade was to have or at least part of the forces were to have an offensive role to play, a very active role in the operation with respect to capturing a specific feature, preventing the intervention of enemy reserve forces from Potocari and Srebrenica. So it had an offensive flavour that the brigade was expected to take some significant offensive operations in order to ensure that the 28th Infantry Division could not withdraw forces from one end of the enclave and redeploy them against what would be the main attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's talk about the main flavour of this order. What is the main favour for the Bratunac Brigade, offensive or defensive?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again in this respect it says part of the forces. And in this particular instance it notes that the 1st Infantry Battalion is to join in the attack and coordinate with the execution of the tasks. So given that -- and I'd again have to go back to a map, I think we're looking at an order that the general flavour is offensive in nature, as opposed to defensive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you looked at those points on the map to see how much actual territory we're speaking of this offensive flavour?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd have to go back and look at the map. It's been a while.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, before going back to the map, you should be able, having spent almost six years on this case, to know whether it was a lot of territory that they were supposed to gain, a little bit of territory. I suspect that you would be able to help us out on this without having to refer to the actual map. It's something that you must have done as part of your analysis and synthesis.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I just want to be as clear as possible. I don't believe that, again I don't want to use a broad phrase. I don't believe that there -- it's a significant -- but again looking at this, we're at the role where their primary function is to capture features, less with respect to capturing the features, but to take the actions required to ensure that reserve forces of the 28th Division are not deployed from Potocari. So I mean --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I've got to deconstruct that one. You started with significant and then you went in a different direction. As clearly as possible, is it your understanding that the Bratunac Brigade, given its size and its location, was asked to go on the offensive primarily, or was it just a part of their mandate? Which of the two?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was -- obviously it was a part. It was not a full offensive, and it was, like I said, envisioned in the larger scheme to be a secondary attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. They were supposed to join in?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now -- and you cannot tell us today, as you sit here and without looking at the map, how forward they were supposed to advance, how much terrain they were supposed to gain in this attack?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I'd have to look at a map for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us at least, whether from your memory, what the terrain would have been like, the terrain that they were designated to capture or attack? Do you know what the -- how -- its features. Was it level? Was it hilly? Was it wooded? Do you know any of it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, to the west of the Bratunac Brigade -- Bratunac to Potocari road, it is very hilly terrain. It is wooded. It is mined. Going to the east of that road, the terrain is extremely hilly, very vertical, and would be very difficult -- it's a very difficult task to launch operations in that terrain. Again, I'd prefer to go off a map on this one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I take it at one point you did go on the map and you did plot it out, and if so we would find it on that well-documented and highly footnoted narrative of yours, wouldn't we?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. Because for the purpose of my narrative --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would be enough. I think we understood each other --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. If he's going to be criticised for not having something in his report I think he should be allowed to explain --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- as he was starting to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, do not speak while the Prosecution is making an objection. I think that's the -- you have to show some politeness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I agree with you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I would like to Prosecutor not to interrupt me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: This is his right. He has the right to stand up, to object.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He has to let me finish first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: He said that he will let the witness finish first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I apologise. I truly apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, again please accept my apologies. Give us a full, complete, thorough answer as to why you probably or why you didn't put this into your report and leave it at that, either the narrative or the other one, the first one and the revised versions.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an economy measure insomuch as while I would have been fascinated to go through all the dynamics of the day-to-day operation, given the fact that the purpose of the report has to do with the linkage to known crime scenes, it was not something, while I would have been very personally interested in doing, didn't appear to have any relevance with respect to a day-to-day accounting of a military operation, which by all accounts was conducted in the confines of the law of war. That's why it never really made it in there from that perspective.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Fair enough. If I understand you in my parlance, from your point of view the attack on Srebrenica was not in violation of any international law that you're aware of?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand that there were some portions of the attack, that there are questions as to whether they may or may not have been lawful under some technical things. For example, some sporadic shelling incidents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the attack itself. I'm not talking about the manner in which the attack was carried out. The attack itself on Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I agree. And I don't believe it's ever been implied that it's charged as such.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to make sure we are clear on that. Did you by any chance in your analysis and synthesis determine whether the Bratunac Brigade effectively carried out the orders as they are described in this particular order, that is, the July 2nd order that was issued or signed by Major General Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. With respect to particularly the operations of the 1st Battalion, how the operation unfolded with respect to Bratunac was not carried out that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, it wasn't carried -- so -- just to make sure that I'm clear. The Bratunac Brigade did not carry out the order or carry out their tasks as they were ordered pursuant to this particular document, which is an order from the commander of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I mean, clearly somewhere down the line, and again it's reflected in the July 5 document, there was a modification in the role that the Bratunac Brigade was to play in this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's look to that one then. I believe it has been marked for identification purposes as P406. Is that the one that we're talking about, Mr. Butler?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you could, as plainly as possible, tell us how did this order from July 5, 1995, by the brigade commander of the Bratunac Brigade, how this order deviated from the order that had been given to him from his commander of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very broadly it puts -- instead of having some of the other battalions launching larger operations, it limits the offensive tasks to the 3rd Infantry Battalion -- and I want to get to the right paragraph on this one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just give us the general.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It limits the offensive tasks of the 3rd Infantry Battalion to carry out a secondary -- or an attack along the secondary axis in order to support the main effort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just in plain, ordinary, pedestrian English, what exactly are you telling us? We have the one order and then we have the other order. Are you saying that rather than put his forces on the offensive, he placed them on the defensive, more or less is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. What I'm saying is that somewhere between the 2nd and the 5th, there was a refinement in the mission of the Bratunac Brigade, in part based on their combat capabilities to conduct that mission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did this change -- we know that there's a change. I guess what I'm trying to get at, did this order become more aggressive in a sense for the Bratunac Brigade that they were going to be a more active participant, or were they going to be a more passive participant? Which of the two?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think with those two choices, it's more of a passive participation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, would you like to characterise it in another fashion?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, with respect to, again, the objectives of some of the battalions on the northern portion, rather than actively seeking to take terrain features, they were just to conduct activities to hold the enemy in place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, remain static and if they came into contact do something, otherwise just stay put?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not quite that simple, because there are obviously other ways to hold the enemy in place, fixing them through fire support, limited movements out of the line. So I mean, it's not straight static defence, and again as reflected in the tasks, the battalions did do some fire support-related functions in order to fix the enemy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But they didn't advance to gain ground?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, other than the units of the 3rd Battalion during the course of the conduct of the attack, the other battalions did not advance to gain ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And even the 3rd Battalion, is it not a fact, didn't do a whole lot either in reality during those days?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it was, perhaps, a company or a two-company size that was actually conducting that secondary attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Just for comparison purposes, and I think this will be the last -- if we could make this the last segment, because I want to go into detail on this order. But if we were to compare this order for the Bratunac Brigade that was drafted by the commander based on the tasks given to him from the Drina Corps commander on July 2nd, if we were to compare this one from the one, say, from the Zvornik Brigade drafted by, I believe it was, Colonel Pandurevic or lieutenant colonel, I believe he might have been at that point. And in fact, I believe the date on that one is the same date as the order itself, 2nd July 1995. Would it not be fair to say that Pandurevic in his order gave himself a greater role than was envisaged by his commander in his order of July 2nd?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether he gave himself a greater role in that respect. I would actually have to look at those two documents. I don't think I've analysed them in that respect. It could be something I could look at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect to the formation of what he's supposed to take with him from Zvornik to lead the attack, that might clue you in a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're at a point where I would prefer if we could break. We have a couple minutes left, but if it's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll break now and we'll resume at 9.00 in the same courtroom tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
